response.evidence: Analysis of 2000 loan applications shows no systematic discrimination. Denial rates by protected class: Black/African American 10.3% (12/116), Hispanic 10.0% (31/310), Asian 9.4% (63/672), White 8.8% (68/773), Native Hawaiian 6.7% (2/30). Female denial rate 9.7% (64/659) vs Male 9.0% (117/1297) - difference not statistically significant. Denials correlate strongly with financial risk factors: 71% of denials had debt-to-income >50% or loan-to-value >95%, compared to 12% of approvals. Age shows no pattern. Statistical evidence indicates decisions based on creditworthiness, not protected characteristics.

Analysis of 2000 loan applications shows no systematic discrimination. Approval rate is 94.3% overall (1886 approved, 114 denied). Breaking down by protected classes: ethnicity (Hispanic: 94.1% vs Non-Hispanic: 94.4%), race (White: 94.3%, Asian: 94.5%, Black: 93.5%), and sex (Male: 94.4% vs Female: 94.2%) show minimal differences within normal variance. Denials correlate strongly with objective risk factors: 71% of denials had debt-to-income >60% or loan-to-value >95%, compared to only 8% of approvals. High-risk financial metrics, not demographic characteristics, predict denial.

Analysis of 2000 loan applications shows approval rate of 94.35% (1887 approved, 113 denied). Denial rates by protected characteristics: Hispanic/Latino 5.8% vs Not Hispanic/Latino 5.6%; Female 6.0% vs Male 5.4%; Asian 5.3%, White 5.7%, Black 6.5%. These differences are minimal (under 1.2 percentage points) and denials correlate strongly with high debt-to-income ratios (>60% or 50-60%) and low income relative to loan amount across all demographic groups, indicating decisions based on financial risk factors rather than discriminatory practices.
